interface.title: Dispersion Equation for Magneto-Rossby and Alfvén Waves (Streamlit app, page title 'Sectoral Magneto-Rossby Dispersion Equation')
interface.field: Solar physics / helioseismology: magnetohydrodynamic waves in a rotating star (Rossby, magneto-Rossby and Alfvén waves)
interface.stage_of_work: Theory exploration and parameter study before comparing with observations; produces model curves for later analysis
interface.what_it_is_for: Set rotation, radius, density and one or more magnetic field strengths, then see and export how the HD Rossby, fast/slow magneto-Rossby and Alfvén dispersion branches ν(m) change across azimuthal order m.

data.note: Nothing is uploaded or loaded. All curves are computed from the sidebar settings on every rerun. The defaults are Ω=456 nHz, R=6.96e8 m, ρ=1e-2 kg m^-3, m=1..30, B=0,10,30,50 G. B=0 gives only the HD Rossby curve, and each B>0 adds Fast, Slow, Alfvén+ and Alfvén− curves. The exported file is magnetic_dispersion_curves.csv with columns curve, B_G, m, nu_nHz. It holds only the curve families currently toggled on in Plot toggles.

features.name: Multi-value parameter list with presets and free-text fallback
features.general: Pick a set of values for a control parameter from named presets, or type your own comma-separated list. Unparseable input shows an error message and falls back to defaults. Each value becomes its own family of curves.
features.specific: The 'B presets' selectbox (Custom, 0,10,30,50, 0,5,10,20,50,100, 0..100 step 10). 'Custom' reveals the 'Custom B list in Gauss' text box. Bad input shows the red error box 'Could not parse B list. Using [0, 10, 30, 50].' Each B>0 adds Fast/Slow/Alfvén legend entries.
steps: Open the presets dropdown
Choose a preset, or choose Custom
Type a comma-separated list into the text box and press Enter
Read the new curve families in the legend and table, or the error message if parsing failed
serves_tasks: Choose several values of the control parameter to compare at once

features.name: Curve-family visibility toggles linked to plot, table and export
features.general: Checkboxes switch whole families of model curves on and off, and the plot legend, the results table and the exported file follow together
features.specific: Plot toggles: Show HD Rossby baseline, Show fast/slow magneto-Rossby branches, Show Alfvén branch. Hidden families drop out of the figure, the Data table and the Download CSV file.
steps: Uncheck a family
Read the reduced plot and legend
Check the table and see the hidden family's rows are gone
Re-check to restore it
serves_tasks: Show only some families of curves to isolate one behaviour

features.name: Axis-window range sliders for a static plot
features.general: Two-handle range sliders set the x and y limits of a static chart, so you can zoom into a region without interactive chart tools
features.specific: Axes: 'm limit' (0–60) and 'ν limit (nHz)' (−5000…5000) range sliders redraw the matplotlib figure with new xlim/ylim. Arrow keys move 1 unit and dragging moves coarsely. The m limit resets to the m max when the mode range changes.
steps: Drag the upper or lower handle of the m-limit slider
Drag (or arrow-key) the ν-limit handles
Read the zoomed figure
Widen the handles again to zoom back out
serves_tasks: Zoom into a region of the plot and enlarge it for closer reading

features.name: Live parameter sweep driving a computed family-of-curves plot
features.general: Numeric inputs for the physical constants and the sample range recompute and redraw every model curve at once, with the current parameters printed in the figure title
features.specific: Rotation Ω, Solar radius R⊙ and Density ρ number inputs, plus azimuthal order m min/max, recompute ν(m) for every branch. The subtitle shows 'ρ = …, Ω/(2π) = … nHz'.
steps: Type a new value (or press +/−) in a background parameter
Press Enter to rerun
Compare the new branch shapes and subtitle with the previous figure
Change the m min/max to extend or shorten the scan
serves_tasks: Set the background physical parameters and see how the model responds
Choose the range of mode numbers to compute
Compare the perturbed model branches against the unperturbed baseline as the control parameter and background change

features.name: Tidy long-format CSV export of the shown curves
features.general: The computed curves are saved as tidy rows (family, parameter value, x, y), one row per point, containing only the families currently shown, ready for use elsewhere
features.specific: The 'Download CSV' button saves magnetic_dispersion_curves.csv with columns curve, B_G, m, nu_nHz, built from the same dataframe as the Data table. The Alfvén branch is stored as two curves, 'Alfvén +' and 'Alfvén −'.
steps: Set the Plot toggles to the families you want
Click Download CSV
Open magnetic_dispersion_curves.csv and read rows by curve and B_G
serves_tasks: Save the computed curves as a table file for later analysis

features.name: Colour-by-parameter, line-style-by-family curve encoding
features.general: Each value of the control parameter gets its own colour and each wave family its own line style, so many families can share one figure and legend; a symmetric ± pair shares one legend entry
features.specific: One colour per B; black solid HD Rossby, dotted Fast, solid Slow, dash-dot Alfvén, with one legend entry for the Alfvén ± pair per B.
steps: Choose several B values
Find a B by its colour in the legend
Tell fast, slow and Alfvén apart by line style within that colour
Compare each against the black HD Rossby line
serves_tasks: Compare the perturbed model branches against the unperturbed baseline as the control parameter and background change
